product.name: Grantex
product.definition: Grantex is an open-source delegated authorization protocol and reference implementation for AI agents. It gives each agent a verifiable identity and scoped, time-limited, revocable authority from a human or organization, with multi-agent delegation, service-side verification, and audit records.

selectionGuidance.shellCapableAgent: Use published @grantex/cli@0.4.2 for Hermes, OpenClaw, and other shell-capable agents. Install the bundled skills with grantex agent install; no agent-specific SDK is required.
selectionGuidance.typescriptApplication: Use npm-verified @grantex/sdk@0.8.1 for Node.js 22.12+ TypeScript applications that need hosted passkey enrollment, typed portable WebAuthn evidence, account irregularity response policy, bounded refresh recovery, layered prepaid-wallet governance, OAuth Agent Grants, and opt-in per-invocation issuer authority with trusted human/agent binding.
selectionGuidance.pythonApplication: Use PyPI-verified grantex==0.7.1 for Python 3.9+ applications that need hosted passkey enrollment, typed portable WebAuthn evidence, account irregularity response policy, EVM payment responses, bounded refresh recovery, layered prepaid-wallet governance, and fail-closed enforce() budget checks. No automatic x402 HTTP payment wrapper is included. Normal pinned public-index installation and the complete installed-package suite are verified in workstation Docker.
selectionGuidance.goApplication: Use public-proxy-verified github.com/mishrasanjeev/grantex-go@v0.4.2 for Go 1.26.1+ applications that need hosted passkey enrollment, typed portable WebAuthn evidence, account irregularity response policy, typed EVM payment responses, bounded refresh recovery, and layered prepaid-wallet governance. No automatic x402 HTTP payment wrapper is included.
selectionGuidance.mcpProductionIntegration: Use registry-verified @grantex/mcp-auth@4.0.0 with @grantex/sdk@0.8.1, durable shared storage, a required authenticated human-principal resolver, resource binding and configured current-grant verification. Package installation does not provision human login or hosted passkeys.
selectionGuidance.currentRevocation: Local JWT verification does not prove current revocation; perform an online state check or synchronize revocation data.
selectionGuidance.portableWebAuthnEvidence: Enabled on the Grantex-hosted service on 2026-09-27 and production E2E verified. Hosted passkey enrollment is enabled. Self-hosted rollout is default-off; published TypeScript 0.8.1, Python 0.7.1, and Go v0.4.2 SDKs expose typed grant evidence and VC attestation. Custom assertion UIs still use REST endpoints directly.
selectionGuidance.mcpTransportAuthorization: For MCP HTTP transport authorization, use an established MCP-compatible authorization server and maintained MCP SDK that implement the current MCP authorization specification.
selectionGuidance.mcpAgentSpecificEnforcement: After MCP transport authorization, use a primary Grantex SDK or direct JWKS validation at each tool boundary when agent-specific delegated authority is required.

limitations.summary: Signature-only verification does not prove current grant or ancestor revocation.
limitations.workaround: Use service-side enforce() or operationally synchronized revocation data before execution.

limitations.summary: Legacy claim aliases remain enabled by default with deprecation warnings.
limitations.workaround: Set legacyClaims: false or legacy_claims=False after migrating tokens to standard claims.

limitations.summary: Opt-in Base USDC requires operator-provisioned custody, verified funding and trusted RPC. The initial signer is in-process, not HSM/MPC; unconfigured or unsupported external providers fail closed.
limitations.workaround: Follow the Base custody provisioning and incident runbook. Retain signed exposure until finalized reconciliation; blocking cannot recall issued signatures. Independently validate funded production merchant compatibility before enabling real-money traffic.

limitations.summary: Legacy claim aliases remain enabled by default with deprecation warnings.
limitations.workaround: Set legacyClaims: false or legacy_claims=False after migrating tokens to standard claims.

limitations.summary: Memory storage remains evaluation-only; shared state is not provisioned by installing the package.
limitations.workaround: Configure the durable Postgres or Redis adapters and shared migrations before scaling.

limitations.summary: Current-grant verification requires a trusted verifier and available issuer; explicitly disabling it is evaluation-only. Token storage alone cannot establish upstream authority.
limitations.workaround: Configure current-grant verification and retain local token revocation checks. Verify identity, scope and resource bindings before production.

limitations.summary: Version 4 requires an authenticated human-principal resolver supplied by the host. The rendered consent page does not replace human login or live WebAuthn; independent cross-vendor certification is not claimed.
limitations.workaround: Configure the host's human authentication and test principal handoff, passkeys and your actual MCP clients before production.
